nodes.description: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss beginning in adulthood and progressing over decades, often asymmetrically in an individual. In 111 p.Pro51Ser carriers hearing decline began at about 38 years in women and 46 in men on regression against age-referenced norms; the authors attribute the sex difference mainly to stricter male reference limits. Onset is allele dependent (second or third decade for p.Phe121Ser). Variants outside the LCCL domain were associated with more severe hearing loss earlier in life in a combined East Asian and European audioprofile analysis, whereas a meta-analysis found LCCL variants to progress more.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in a novel cochlear gene cause DFNA9, a human nonsyndromic deafness with vestibular dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: DFNA9 is an autosomal dominant, nonsyndromic, progressive sensorineural hearing loss with vestibular pathology.

evidence.snippet: Pure-tone thresholds deteriorated by about 2-7 dB per year (mean 3.8 dB per year) in a variable, often asymmetrical, fashion.

evidence.snippet: Variants affecting the LCCL domain of cochlin generally lead to more progression of hearing loss when compared to variants affecting the other domains.

nodes.description: Experimental. RNase H gapmer antisense oligonucleotides against the c.151C>T variant or allele-specific intronic variants degraded mutant COCH minigene transcripts in cultured cells; the best reduced mutant transcript by 60% without lowering wild-type transcript, but allele specificity fell at higher concentrations. The rationale rests on the non-haploinsufficiency mechanism. The cited work is in cultured cells only; a genomically humanized c.151C>T mouse was built for testing sequence-specific therapies in vivo.

evidence.reference_title: AON-based degradation of c.151C>T mutant COCH transcripts associated with dominantly inherited hearing impairment DFNA9.
evidence.snippet: The most potent AON, directed against the c.151C>T mutation, was able to induce a 60% decrease in mutant COCH transcripts without affecting wild-type COCH transcript levels.

evidence.reference_title: AON-based degradation of c.151C>T mutant COCH transcripts associated with dominantly inherited hearing impairment DFNA9.
evidence.snippet: Allele specificity decreased when increasing concentrations of AON were delivered to the cells.

evidence.snippet: Overall, our approach proved beneficial in eliminating potential adverse events of genomic humanization of mouse genes, and provides us with a model in which sequence-specific therapies directed against the human mutant COCH alle can be investigated.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in a novel cochlear gene cause DFNA9, a human nonsyndromic deafness with vestibular dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: Here we report three missense mutations in human COCH (previously described as Coch5b2), a novel cochlear gene, in three unrelated kindreds with DFNA9.

evidence.reference_title: A Pro51Ser mutation in the COCH gene is associated with late onset autosomal dominant progressive sensorineural hearing loss with vestibular defects.
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis revealed a 208C-->T mutation in the COCH gene, resulting in a Pro51Ser substitution in the predicted protein in all affected individuals of the family but not in unaffected family members and 200 control individuals.

evidence.reference_title: AON-based degradation of c.151C>T mutant COCH transcripts associated with dominantly inherited hearing impairment DFNA9.
evidence.snippet: The c.151C>T founder mutation in COCH is a frequent cause of late-onset, dominantly inherited hearing impairment and vestibular dysfunction (DFNA9) in the Dutch/Belgian population.

nodes.description: Knock-in of the human DFNA9 p.Gly88Glu allele. Vestibular evoked potential thresholds are raised at all ages tested while auditory thresholds rise only at 21 months, when four of eight homozygotes had absent ABRs at all frequencies tested and two of three heterozygotes at three of four frequencies. Acellular cochlin-containing deposits form in the interossicular joints, as in human temporal bones.

evidence.reference_title: A targeted Coch missense mutation: a knock-in mouse model for DFNA9 late-onset hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: At 21 months, four of eight Coch(G88E/G88E) mice had absent ABRs at all frequencies tested and two of three Coch(G88E)(/+) mice had absent ABRs at three of four frequencies tested.

nodes.description: For severe to profound loss. In a retrospective comparison of 56 p.Pro51Ser recipients with matched postlingually deafened controls, speech perception and quality of life improved similarly and remained stable to five years; better preoperative aided speech perception predicted better outcome, which the authors read as favouring earlier implantation.

evidence.reference_title: Performance Results and Timing of Cochlear Implantation in Patients With DFNA9 (p.Pro51Ser).
evidence.snippet: CI provides durable, noninferior outcomes in DFNA9 patients compared with controls.

evidence.snippet: The phoneme scores significantly improved from 35% (IQR 11-50) pre-implantation to 84% (IQR 76-90) one year post-implantation.

nodes.description: The histological hallmark of DFNA9: acellular, homogeneous eosinophilic deposits in the spiral ligament, spiral limbus, distal osseous spiral lamina and the stroma beneath the vestibular neuroepithelium, which immunostain for cochlin. All examined DFNA9 temporal bones also carried deposits in the tympanic membrane and the incudomalleal and incudostapedial joints, and one patient with a vWFA2 variant had cochlin aggregates in both external auditory canals. The composition of deposits varies with site.

nodes.description: Attacks of vertigo, sometimes with nausea and vomiting, which together with tinnitus, aural fullness and fluctuating hearing can meet clinical criteria for Menière's disease. More than a quarter of patients in three COCH families had such symptoms. No COCH exon 4 or 5 variants were found in 30 patients with sporadic definite Menière's disease, so the overlap appears clinical rather than genetic.

evidence.snippet: In all three families with hearing loss and imbalance problems, >25% of the patients showed additional symptoms, including episodes of vertigo, tinnitus, aural fullness and hearing loss.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a heterozygous germline missense or in-frame variant in COCH, clustered in the LCCL domain (for example p.Pro51Ser, p.Gly88Glu, p.Phe121Ser) and less often in the vWFA domains (for example p.Phe527Cys, p.Ile541Phe). Mouse and human evidence argue against haploinsufficiency: heterozygous Coch-null mice have normal hearing while heterozygous G88E knock-in mice do not, and a heterozygous human frameshift allele (p.Cys50Leufs*8) was carried by a parent with normal hearing. Whether dominant alleles act by interfering with wild-type cochlin or by a toxic property of the mutant protein is not resolved, and may differ between alleles, so `functional_impact_category` is left unset.

nodes.description: The fibrocytes of the spiral ligament and spiral limbus, and the stromal cells of the crista ampullaris, are where COCH is expressed. In affected temporal bones these cells are absent or markedly reduced. Cochlin remains abundant in the tissue even where the fibrocytes that made it have atrophied. The functional consequence of fibrocyte loss for cochlear homeostasis in DFNA9 has not been measured, so no edge is drawn from this node to the hearing phenotype.
